    Deprecated.

    Constructs a [`UnicodeEscaper`](UnicodeEscaper.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate") for the specified range. This is
    the underlying method for the other constructors/builders. The `below`
    and `above` boundaries are inclusive when `between` is
    `true` and exclusive when it is `false`.

    Parameters:
    :   `below` - int value representing the lowest code point boundary.
    :   `above` - int value representing the highest code point boundary.
    :   `between` - whether to escape between the boundaries or outside them.

---

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public class [AggregateTranslator](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/translate/AggregateTranslator.html#line-33)
extends [CharSequenceTranslator](CharSequenceTranslator.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate")

Deprecated.

As of [3.6](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-lang/changes-report.html#a3.6), use Apache Commons Text
[AggregateTranslator](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-text/javadocs/api-release/org/apache/commons/text/translate/AggregateTranslator.html).

Executes a sequence of translators one after the other. Execution ends whenever
the first translator consumes code points from the input.

Since:
:   3.0

* ## Method Details

  * ### translate

    public int [translate](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/translate/AggregateTranslator.html#line-52)([CharSequence](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") input,
    int index,
    [Writer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Writer.html "class or interface in java.io") out)
    throws [IOException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io")

    Deprecated.

    The first translator to consume code points from the input is the 'winner'.
    Execution stops with the number of consumed code points being returned.
    Translate a set of code points, represented by an int index into a CharSequence,
    into another set of code points. The number of code points consumed must be returned,
    and the only IOExceptions thrown must be from interacting with the Writer so that
    the top level API may reliably ignore StringWriter IOExceptions.

    Specified by:
    :   `translate` in class `CharSequenceTranslator`

    Parameters:
    :   `input` - CharSequence that is being translated.
    :   `index` - int representing the current point of translation.
    :   `out` - Writer to translate the text to.

    Returns:
    :   int count of code points consumed.

    Throws:
    :   `IOException` - if and only if the Writer produces an IOException.

# All Packages

Package Summary

Package

Description

[org.apache.commons.lang3](org/apache/commons/lang3/package-summary.html)

Provides highly reusable utility methods, chiefly concerned with adding value to the [`java.lang`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/package-summary.html) classes.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.arch](org/apache/commons/lang3/arch/package-summary.html)

Provides classes to work with the values of the os.arch system property.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.builder](org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/package-summary.html)

Provides classes to create consistent `equals(Object)`, `toString()`, `hashCode()`, and `compareTo(Object)` methods.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.compare](org/apache/commons/lang3/compare/package-summary.html)

Provides classes to work with the [`Comparable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Comparable.html "class or interface in java.lang") and [`Comparator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Comparator.html "class or interface in java.util") interfaces.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent](org/apache/commons/lang3/concurrent/package-summary.html)

Provides support classes for multi-threaded programming.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent.locks](org/apache/commons/lang3/concurrent/locks/package-summary.html)

Provides support classes for multi-threaded programming.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.event](org/apache/commons/lang3/event/package-summary.html)

Provides some useful event-based utilities.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.exception](org/apache/commons/lang3/exception/package-summary.html)

Provides functionality for Exceptions.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.function](org/apache/commons/lang3/function/package-summary.html)

Provides functional interfaces to complement those in `java.lang.function` and utilities for working with Java
8 lambdas.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.math](org/apache/commons/lang3/math/package-summary.html)

Provides [`java.math`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/math/package-summary.html) extensions for business mathematical classes.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.mutable](org/apache/commons/lang3/mutable/package-summary.html)

Provides typed mutable wrappers to primitive values and Object.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect](org/apache/commons/lang3/reflect/package-summary.html)

Provides high-level uses of the `java.lang.reflect` APIs.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.stream](org/apache/commons/lang3/stream/package-summary.html)

Provides utility classes to complement those in [`java.util.stream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/package-summary.html).

[org.apache.commons.lang3.text](org/apache/commons/lang3/text/package-summary.html)

**Deprecated**: Provides classes for handling and manipulating text, partly as an extension to [`java.text`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/package-summary.html).

[org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate](org/apache/commons/lang3/text/translate/package-summary.html)

**Deprecated**: Provides text translation routines from a set of smaller building blocks.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.time](org/apache/commons/lang3/time/package-summary.html)

Provides classes and methods to work with dates and durations.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple](org/apache/commons/lang3/tuple/package-summary.html)

Provides tuple classes, both mutable and immutable [`Pair`](org/apache/commons/lang3/tuple/Pair.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple") and [`Triple`](org/apache/commons/lang3/tuple/Triple.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple").

[org.apache.commons.lang3.util](org/apache/commons/lang3/util/package-summary.html)

Provides classes that work with the Java [`java.util`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/package-summary.html) package.

# Uses of Package org.apache.commons.lang3.function

Packages that use [org.apache.commons.lang3.function](package-summary.html)

Package

Description

[org.apache.commons.lang3](#org.apache.commons.lang3)

Provides highly reusable utility methods, chiefly concerned with adding value to the [`java.lang`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/package-summary.html) classes.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.builder](#org.apache.commons.lang3.builder)

Provides classes to create consistent `equals(Object)`, `toString()`, `hashCode()`, and `compareTo(Object)` methods.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent](#org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent)

Provides support classes for multi-threaded programming.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent.locks](#org.apache.commons.lang3.concurrent.locks)

Provides support classes for multi-threaded programming.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.event](#org.apache.commons.lang3.event)

Provides some useful event-based utilities.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.function](#org.apache.commons.lang3.function)

Provides functional interfaces to complement those in `java.lang.function` and utilities for working with Java
8 lambdas.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.stream](#org.apache.commons.lang3.stream)

Provides utility classes to complement those in [`java.util.stream`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/package-summary.html).

[org.apache.commons.lang3.time](#org.apache.commons.lang3.time)

Provides classes and methods to work with dates and durations.

[org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple](#org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple)

Provides tuple classes, both mutable and immutable [`Pair`](../tuple/Pair.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple") and [`Triple`](../tuple/Triple.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.tuple").

Package [org.apache.commons.lang3.function](package-summary.html)

# Class Failable

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.function.Failable

---

public class [Failable](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Failable.html#line-73)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

This class provides utility functions, and classes for working with the `java.util.function` package, or more
generally, with Java 8 lambdas. More specifically, it attempts to address the fact that lambdas are supposed not to
throw Exceptions, at least not checked Exceptions, like instances of [`Exception`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Exception.html "class or interface in java.lang"). This enforces the use of
constructs like:

```
 Consumer<java.lang.reflect.Method> consumer = m -> {
     try {
         m.invoke(o, args);
     } catch (Throwable t) {
         throw Failable.rethrow(t);
     }
 };
```

By replacing a [`Consumer<O>`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Consumer.html "class or interface in java.util.function") with a [`FailableConsumer<O,? extends Throwable>`](FailableConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"), this can be written like follows:

```
 Functions.accept(m -> m.invoke(o, args));
```

Obviously, the second version is much more concise and the spirit of Lambda expressions is met better than the second
version.

Since:
:   3.11

  * ### applyNonNull

    public static <T,
    R,
    E extends [Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")> R [applyNonNull](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Failable.html#line-205)(T value,
    [FailableFunction](FailableFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<? super T,? extends R,E> mapper)
    throws E

    Applies a value to a function if the value isn't `null`, otherwise the method returns `null`. If the value isn't `null` then return the
    result of the applying function.

    ```
     Failable.applyNonNull("a", String::toUpperCase)  = "A"
     Failable.applyNonNull(null, String::toUpperCase) = null
     Failable.applyNonNull("a", s -> null)            = null
    ```

    Useful when working with expressions that may return `null` as it allows a single-line expression without using temporary local variables or

    Applies values to a chain of functions, where a `null` can short-circuit each step. A function is only applied if the previous value is not
    `null`, otherwise this method returns `null`.

    ```
     Failable.applyNonNull(" a ", String::toUpperCase, String::trim) = "A"
     Failable.applyNonNull(null, String::toUpperCase, String::trim)  = null
     Failable.applyNonNull(" a ", s -> null, String::trim)           = null
     Failable.applyNonNull(" a ", String::toUpperCase, s -> null)    = null
    ```

    Useful when working with expressions that may return `null` as it allows a single-line expression without using temporary local variables or
    evaluating expressions twice. Provides an alternative to using [`Optional`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Optional.html "class or interface in java.util") that is shorter and has less allocation.

    :   `E2` - The type of thrown exception or error by the second function.

  * ### rethrow

    public static [RuntimeException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/RuntimeException.html "class or interface in java.lang") [rethrow](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Failable.html#line-516)([Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang") throwable)

    Rethrows a [`Throwable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang") as an unchecked exception. If the argument is already unchecked, namely a
    [`RuntimeException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/RuntimeException.html "class or interface in java.lang") or [`Error`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Error.html "class or interface in java.lang") then the argument will be rethrown without modification. If the
    exception is [`IOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/IOException.html "class or interface in java.io") then it will be wrapped into a [`UncheckedIOException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/UncheckedIOException.html "class or interface in java.io"). In every other
    cases the exception will be wrapped into a `UndeclaredThrowableException`

    Note that there is a declared return type for this method, even though it never returns. The reason for that is
    to support the usual pattern:

    ```
     throw rethrow(myUncheckedException);
    ```

    instead of just calling the method. This pattern may help the Java compiler to recognize that at that point an
    exception will be thrown and the code flow analysis will not demand otherwise mandatory commands that could
    follow the method call, like a `return` statement from a value returning method.

    Parameters:
    :   `throwable` - The throwable to rethrow possibly wrapped into an unchecked exception

    Returns:
    :   Never returns anything, this method never terminates normally.

    public static <T> [Streams.FailableStream](../stream/Streams.FailableStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.stream")<T> [stream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Failable.html#line-577)([Stream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/Stream.html "class or interface in java.util.stream")<T> stream)

    Converts the given stream into a [`Streams.FailableStream`](../stream/Streams.FailableStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.stream"). The [`Streams.FailableStream`](../stream/Streams.FailableStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.stream") consists of the same
    elements, than the input stream. However, failable lambdas, like [`FailablePredicate`](FailablePredicate.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"),
    [`FailableFunction`](FailableFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"), and [`FailableConsumer`](FailableConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function") may be applied, rather than [`Predicate`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Predicate.html "class or interface in java.util.function"),
    [`Function`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function"), [`Consumer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Consumer.html "class or interface in java.util.function"), etc.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - The streams element type.

    Parameters:
    :   `stream` - The stream, which is being converted into a [`Streams.FailableStream`](../stream/Streams.FailableStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.stream").

    Returns:
    :   The created [`Streams.FailableStream`](../stream/Streams.FailableStream.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.stream").

  * ### tryWithResources

    [@SafeVarargs](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/SafeVarargs.html "class or interface in java.lang")
    public static void [tryWithResources](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Failable.html#line-629)([FailableRunnable](FailableRunnable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<? extends [Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")> action,
    [FailableConsumer](FailableConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<[Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang"),? extends [Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")> errorHandler,
    [FailableRunnable](FailableRunnable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<? extends [Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")>... resources)

    A simple try-with-resources implementation, that can be used, if your objects do not implement the
    [`AutoCloseable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/AutoCloseable.html "class or interface in java.lang") interface. The method executes the `action`. The method guarantees, that *all*
    the `resources` are being executed, in the given order, afterwards, and regardless of success, or failure.
    If either the original action, or any of the resource action fails, then the *first* failure (AKA
    [`Throwable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")) is rethrown. Example use:

    ```
     final FileInputStream fis = new FileInputStream("my.file");
     Functions.tryWithResources(useInputStream(fis), null, () -> fis.close());
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `action` - The action to execute. This object *will* always be invoked.
    :   `errorHandler` - An optional error handler, which will be invoked finally, if any error occurred. The error
        handler will receive the first error, AKA [`Throwable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang").
    :   `resources` - The resource actions to execute. *All* resource actions will be invoked, in the given
        order. A resource action is an instance of [`FailableRunnable`](FailableRunnable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"), which will be executed.

    See Also:
    :   * [`tryWithResources(FailableRunnable, FailableRunnable...)`](#tryWithResources(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableRunnable,org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableRunnable...))

# Class MethodInvokers

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.function.MethodInvokers

---

public final class [MethodInvokers](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/MethodInvokers.html#line-71)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Converts [`Method`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/reflect/Method.html "class or interface in java.lang.reflect") objects to lambdas.

More specifically, produces instances of single-method interfaces which redirect calls to methods; see
[`asInterfaceInstance(Class, Method)`](#asInterfaceInstance(java.lang.Class,java.lang.reflect.Method)).

## Calling supplier methods with no arguments

If the interface's single-method defines no arguments, use [`asFunction(Method)`](#asFunction(java.lang.reflect.Method)) and then apply the function
passing in the object to receive the method call.

For example to invoke [`String.length()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#length-- "class or interface in java.lang"):

```
 final Method method = String.class.getMethod("length");
 final Function<String, Integer> function = MethodInvokers.asFunction(method);
 assertEquals(3, function.apply("ABC"));
```

## Calling function methods with one argument

If the interface's single-method defines one argument, use [`asBiFunction(Method)`](#asBiFunction(java.lang.reflect.Method)) and then apply the function
passing in the object to receive the method call. The second argument to the function is the only argument to the
method.

For example to invoke [`String.charAt(int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#charAt-int- "class or interface in java.lang"):

```
 final Method method = String.class.getMethod("charAt", int.class);
 final BiFunction<String, Integer, Character> function = MethodInvokers.asBiFunction(method);
 assertEquals('C', function.apply("ABC", 2));
```

Since:
:   3.13.0

    Produces a [`BiFunction`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/BiFunction.html "class or interface in java.util.function") for a given a *function* Method. You call the BiFunction with two arguments: (1)
    the object receiving the method call, and (2) the method argument. The BiFunction return type must match the method's
    return type.

    For example to invoke [`String.charAt(int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#charAt-int- "class or interface in java.lang"):

    ```
     final Method method = String.class.getMethod("charAt", int.class);
     final BiFunction<String, Integer, Character> function = MethodInvokers.asBiFunction(method);
     assertEquals('C', function.apply("ABC", 2));
    ```

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - the type of the first argument to the function: The type containing the method.
    :   `U` - the type of the second argument to the function: the method argument type.
    :   `R` - the type of the result of the function: The method return type.

    Parameters:
    :   `method` - the method to invoke.

    Returns:
    :   a correctly-typed wrapper for the given target.

    public static <T,
    R> R [apply](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Functions.html#line-41)([Function](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<T,R> function,

    Applies the [`Function`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function") on the object if the function is not `null`. Otherwise, does nothing and returns `null`.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - the type of the argument the function applies.
    :   `R` - the type of the result the function returns.

    Parameters:
    :   `function` - the function to apply.
    :   `object` - the object to apply the function.

    Returns:
    :   the value the function returns if the function is not `null`; `null` otherwise.

    Since:
    :   3.15.0
  * ### applyNonNull

    public static <T,
    R> R [applyNonNull](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Functions.html#line-68)(T value,
    [Function](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<? super T,? extends R> mapper)

    Applies a value to a function if the value isn't `null`, otherwise the method returns `null`. If the value isn't `null` then return the
    result of the applying function.

    ```
     Functions.applyNonNull("a", String::toUpperCase)  = "A"
     Functions.applyNonNull(null, String::toUpperCase) = null
     Functions.applyNonNull("a", s -> null)            = null
    ```

    Useful when working with expressions that may return `null` as it allows a single-line expression without using temporary local variables or
    evaluating expressions twice. Provides an alternative to using [`Optional`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Optional.html "class or interface in java.util") that is shorter and has less allocation.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - The type of the input of this method and the function.
    :   `R` - The type of the result of the function and this method.

    Parameters:
    :   `value` - The value to apply the function to, may be `null`.
    :   `mapper` - The function to apply, must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   The result of the function (which may be `null`) or `null` if the input value is `null`.

    Since:
    :   3.19.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`applyNonNull(Object, Function, Function)`](#applyNonNull(T,java.util.function.Function,java.util.function.Function))
        * [`applyNonNull(Object, Function, Function, Function)`](#applyNonNull(T,java.util.function.Function,java.util.function.Function,java.util.function.Function))
  * ### applyNonNull

    public static <T,
    U,
    R> R [applyNonNull](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/Functions.html#line-98)(T value1,
    [Function](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<? super T,? extends U> mapper1,
    [Function](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function")<? super U,? extends R> mapper2)

    Applies values to a chain of functions, where a `null` can short-circuit each step. A function is only applied if the previous value is not
    `null`, otherwise this method returns `null`.

    ```
     Functions.applyNonNull(" a ", String::toUpperCase, String::trim) = "A"
     Functions.applyNonNull(null, String::toUpperCase, String::trim)  = null
     Functions.applyNonNull(" a ", s -> null, String::trim)           = null
     Functions.applyNonNull(" a ", String::toUpperCase, s -> null)    = null
    ```

    Useful when working with expressions that may return `null` as it allows a single-line expression without using temporary local variables or
    evaluating expressions twice. Provides an alternative to using [`Optional`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Optional.html "class or interface in java.util") that is shorter and has less allocation.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - The type of the input of this method and the first function.
    :   `U` - The type of the result of the first function and the input to the second function.
    :   `R` - The type of the result of the second function and this method.

    Parameters:
    :   `value1` - The value to apply the functions to, may be `null`.
    :   `mapper1` - The first function to apply, must not be `null`.
    :   `mapper2` - The second function to apply, must not be `null`.

    Returns:
    :   The result of the final function (which may be `null`) or `null` if the input value or any intermediate value is `null`.

    Since:
    :   3.19.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`applyNonNull(Object, Function)`](#applyNonNull(T,java.util.function.Function))
        * [`applyNonNull(Object, Function, Function, Function)`](#applyNonNull(T,java.util.function.Function,java.util.function.Function,java.util.function.Function))

public interface [IntToCharFunction](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/IntToCharFunction.html#line-33)

Represents a function that accepts an int-valued argument and produces a char-valued result. This is the `int`-to-`char` primitive specialization
for [`Function`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function").

This is a [functional interface](package-summary.html) whose functional method is [`applyAsChar(int)`](#applyAsChar(int)).

# Interface TriConsumer<T,U,V>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - type of the first argument
:   `U` - type of the second argument
:   `V` - type of the third argument

Functional Interface:
:   This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.

---

[@FunctionalInterface](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public interface [TriConsumer](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/TriConsumer.html#line-40)<T,U,V>

Represents an operation that accepts three input arguments and returns no result. This is the three-arity
specialization of [`Consumer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Consumer.html "class or interface in java.util.function"). Unlike most other functional interfaces, [`TriConsumer`](TriConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function") is expected to
operate via side effects.

This is a [`FunctionalInterface`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang") whose functional method is [`accept(Object, Object, Object)`](#accept(T,U,V)).

Provenance: Apache Log4j 2.7

Since:
:   3.13.0

# Interface TriFunction<T,U,V,R>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of the first argument to the function
:   `U` - the type of the second argument to the function
:   `V` - the type of the third argument to the function
:   `R` - the type of the result of the function

Functional Interface:
:   This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.

---

[@FunctionalInterface](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public interface [TriFunction](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/function/TriFunction.html#line-38)<T,U,V,R>

Represents a function that accepts three arguments and produces a result. This is the three-arity specialization of
[`Function`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function").

This is a [functional interface](package-summary.html) whose functional method is
[`apply(Object, Object, Object)`](#apply(T,U,V)).

Since:
:   3.12.0

See Also:
:   * [`Function`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/function/Function.html "class or interface in java.util.function")

# Class Validate

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate

---

public class [Validate](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/Validate.html#line-49)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

This class assists in validating arguments. The validation methods are
based along the following principles:

* An invalid `null` argument causes a [`NullPointerException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/NullPointerException.html "class or interface in java.lang").
* A non-`null` argument causes an [`IllegalArgumentException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IllegalArgumentException.html "class or interface in java.lang").
* An invalid index into an array/collection/map/string causes an [`IndexOutOfBoundsException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/IndexOutOfBoundsException.html "class or interface in java.lang").

All exceptions messages are
[format strings](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Formatter.html#syntax)
as defined by the Java platform. For example:

```
 Validate.isTrue(i > 0, "The value must be greater than zero: %d", i);
 Validate.notNull(surname, "The surname must not be %s", null);
```

#ThreadSafe#

:   2.0

    Validates that the argument can be converted to the specified class, if not, throws an exception.

    This method is useful when validating that there will be no casting errors.

    ```
    Validate.isAssignableFrom(SuperClass.class, object.getClass());
    ```

    :   `type` - the class to check, not null.

    Throws:

  * ### isTrue

    public static void [isTrue](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/Validate.html#line-497)(boolean expression)

    Validate that the argument condition is `true`; otherwise
    throwing an exception. This method is useful when validating according
    to an arbitrary boolean expression, such as validating a
    primitive number or using your own custom validation expression.

    ```
     Validate.isTrue(i > 0);
     Validate.isTrue(myObject.isOk());
    ```

    The message of the exception is "The validated expression is
    false".

    Parameters:
    :   `expression` - the boolean expression to check.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if expression is `false`.

    See Also:
    :   * [`isTrue(boolean, String, long)`](#isTrue(boolean,java.lang.String,long))
        * [`isTrue(boolean, String, double)`](#isTrue(boolean,java.lang.String,double))

    public static void [isTrue](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/Validate.html#line-523)(boolean expression,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") message,
    double value)

    Validate that the argument condition is `true`; otherwise
    throwing an exception with the specified message. This method is useful when
    validating according to an arbitrary boolean expression, such as validating a
    primitive number or using your own custom validation expression.

    ```
    Validate.isTrue(d > 0.0, "The value must be greater than zero: %s", d);
    ```

    For performance reasons, the double value is passed as a separate parameter and
    appended to the exception message only in the case of an error.

    Parameters:
    :   `expression` - the boolean expression to check.
    :   `message` - the [`String.format(String, Object...)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#format-java.lang.String-java.lang.Object...- "class or interface in java.lang") exception message if invalid, not null.
    :   `value` - the value to append to the message when invalid.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if expression is `false`.

    See Also:

        * [`isTrue(boolean, String, long)`](#isTrue(boolean,java.lang.String,long))

  * ### noNullElements

    public static <T extends [Iterable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?>> T [noNullElements](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/Validate.html#line-666)(T iterable)

    Validate that the specified argument iterable is neither
    `null` nor contains any elements that are `null`;
    otherwise throwing an exception.

    ```
    Validate.noNullElements(myCollection);
    ```

    If the iterable is `null`, then the message in the exception
    is "The validated object is null".

    If the array has a `null` element, then the message in the
    exception is "The validated iterable contains null element at index:
    " followed by the index.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - the iterable type.

    Parameters:
    :   `iterable` - the iterable to check, validated not null by this method.

    Returns:
    :   the validated iterable (never `null` method for chaining).

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the array is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if an element is `null`.

    See Also:
    :   * [`noNullElements(Iterable, String, Object...)`](#noNullElements(T,java.lang.String,java.lang.Object...))

    Validates that the index is within the bounds of the argument
    collection; otherwise throwing an exception.

    followed by the index.

    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the index is invalid.

    public static void [validState](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/Validate.html#line-1248)(boolean expression)

    Validate that the stateful condition is `true`; otherwise
    throwing an exception. This method is useful when validating according
    to an arbitrary boolean expression, such as validating a
    primitive number or using your own custom validation expression.

    ```
     Validate.validState(field > 0);
     Validate.validState(this.isOk());
    ```

    The message of the exception is "The validated state is
    false".

    Parameters:
    :   `expression` - the boolean expression to check.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - if expression is `false`.

    Since:
    :   3.0

# Class DurationFormatUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.time.DurationFormatUtils

---

public class [DurationFormatUtils](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DurationFormatUtils.html#line-92)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Duration formatting utilities and constants. The following table describes the tokens
used in the pattern language for formatting.

Pattern Tokens

| character | duration element |
| y | years |
| M | months |
| d | days |
| H | hours |
| m | minutes |
| s | seconds |
| S | milliseconds |
| 'text' | arbitrary text content |

**Note: It's not currently possible to include a single-quote in a format.**

Token values are printed using decimal digits.
A token character can be repeated to ensure that the field occupies a certain minimum
size. Values will be left-padded with 0 unless padding is disabled in the method invocation.

Tokens can be marked as optional by surrounding them with brackets [ ]. These tokens will
only be printed if the token value is non-zero. Literals within optional blocks will only be
printed if the preceding non-literal token is non-zero. Leading optional literals will only
be printed if the following non-literal is non-zero.
Multiple optional blocks can be used to group literals with the desired token.

Notes on Optional Tokens:

**Multiple optional tokens without literals can result in impossible to understand output.**

**Patterns where all tokens are optional can produce empty strings.**

See the following examples.

Example Output

| pattern | Duration.ofDays(1) | Duration.ofHours(1) | Duration.ofMinutes(1) | Duration.ZERO |
| d'd'H'h'm'm's's' | 1d0h0m0s | 0d1h0m0s | 0d0h1m0s | 0d0h0m0s |
| d'd'[H'h'm'm']s's' | 1d0s | 0d1h0s | 0d1m0s | 0d0s |
| [d'd'H'h'm'm']s's' | 1d0s | 1h0s | 1m0s | 0s |
| [d'd'H'h'm'm's's'] | 1d | 1h | 1m |  |
| ['{'d'}']HH':'mm | {1}00:00 | 01:00 | 00:01 | 00:00 |
| ['{'dd'}']['<'HH'>']['('mm')'] | {01} | <01> | (00) |  |
| [dHms] | 1 | 1 | 1 |  |

**Note: Optional blocks cannot be nested.**

Since:
:   2.1

    public static [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [formatPeriod](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DurationFormatUtils.html#line-540)(long startMillis,
    long endMillis,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") format,
    boolean padWithZeros,
    [TimeZone](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html "class or interface in java.util") timezone)

    Formats the time gap as a string, using the specified format.
    Padding the left-hand side side of numbers with zeroes is optional and
    the time zone may be specified.

    When calculating the difference between months/days, it chooses to
    calculate months first. So when working out the number of months and
    days between January 15th and March 10th, it choose 1 month and
    23 days gained by choosing January->February = 1 month and then
    calculating days forwards, and not the 1 month and 26 days gained by
    choosing March -> February = 1 month and then calculating days
    backwards.

    For more control, the [Joda-Time](https://www.joda.org/joda-time/)
    library is recommended.

    Parameters:
    :   `startMillis` - the start of the duration
    :   `endMillis` - the end of the duration
    :   `format` - the way in which to format the duration, not null
    :   `padWithZeros` - whether to pad the left-hand side side of numbers with 0's
    :   `timezone` - the millis are defined in

    Returns:
    :   the formatted duration, not null

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if startMillis is greater than endMillis

[@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public abstract class [StrLookup](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrLookup.html#line-46)<V>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Deprecated.

As of [3.6](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-lang/changes-report.html#a3.6), use Apache Commons Text
[StringLookupFactory](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-text/javadocs/api-release/org/apache/commons/text/lookup/StringLookupFactory.html).

Lookup a String key to a String value.

This class represents the simplest form of a string to string map.
It has a benefit over a map in that it can create the result on
demand based on the key.

This class comes complete with various factory methods.
If these do not suffice, you can subclass and implement your own matcher.

For example, it would be possible to implement a lookup that used the
key as a primary key, and looked up the value on demand from the database.

Since:
:   2.2

  * ### lookup

    public abstract [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [lookup](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/text/StrLookup.html#line-185)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") key)

    Deprecated.

    Looks up a String key to a String value.

    The internal implementation may use any mechanism to return the value.
    The simplest implementation is to use a Map. However, virtually any
    implementation is possible.

    For example, it would be possible to implement a lookup that used the
    key as a primary key, and looked up the value on demand from the database
    Or, a numeric based implementation could be created that treats the key
    as an integer, increments the value and return the result as a string -
    converting 1 to 2, 15 to 16 etc.

    The [`lookup(String)`](#lookup(java.lang.String)) method always returns a String, regardless of
    the underlying data, by converting it as necessary. For example:

    ```
     Map<String, Object> map = new HashMap<String, Object>();
     map.put("number", Integer.valueOf(2));
     assertEquals("2", StrLookup.mapLookup(map).lookup("number"));
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `key` - the key to be looked up, may be null.

    Returns:
    :   the matching value, null if no match.

# Class DateUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

---

public class [DateUtils](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-59)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

A suite of utilities surrounding the use of the
[`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") and [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") object.

DateUtils contains a lot of common methods considering manipulations
of Dates or Calendars. Some methods require some extra explanation.
The truncate, ceiling and round methods could be considered the Math.floor(),
Math.ceil() or Math.round versions for dates
This way date-fields will be ignored in bottom-up order.
As a complement to these methods we've introduced some fragment-methods.
With these methods the Date-fields will be ignored in top-down order.
Since a date without a year is not a valid date, you have to decide in what
kind of date-field you want your result, for instance milliseconds or days.

Several methods are provided for adding to [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") objects, of the form
`addXXX(Date date, int amount)`. It is important to note these methods
use a [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") internally (with default time zone and locale) and may
be affected by changes to daylight saving time (DST).

Since:
:   2.0

  * ### DateUtils

    [@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
    public [DateUtils](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-1859)()

    Deprecated.

    TODO Make private in 4.0.

    [`DateUtils`](DateUtils.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.time") instances should NOT be constructed in
    standard programming. Instead, the static methods on the class should
    be used, such as `DateUtils.parseDate(str);`.

    This constructor is public to permit tools that require a JavaBean
    instance to operate.

  * ### ceiling

    public static [Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") [ceiling](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-350)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar,
    int field)

    Gets a date ceiling, leaving the field specified as the most
    significant field.

    For example, if you had the date-time of 28 Mar 2002
    13:45:01.231, if you passed with HOUR, it would return 28 Mar
    2002 14:00:00.000. If this was passed with MONTH, it would
    return 1 Apr 2002 0:00:00.000.

    Parameters:
    :   `calendar` - the date to work with, not null.
    :   `field` - the field from [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") or `SEMI_MONTH`.

    Returns:
    :   the different ceil date, not null.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null`.
    :   `ArithmeticException` - if the year is over 280 million.

    Since:
    :   2.5
  * ### ceiling

  * ### ceiling

    public static [Date](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") [ceiling](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-392)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") date,

    significant field.

    For example, if you had the date-time of 28 Mar 2002
    13:45:01.231, if you passed with HOUR, it would return 28 Mar
    2002 14:00:00.000. If this was passed with MONTH, it would
    return 1 Apr 2002 0:00:00.000.

    Parameters:
    :   `date` - the date to work with, either [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") or [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util"), not null.
    :   `field` - the field from [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") or `SEMI_MONTH`.

    Returns:
    :   the different ceil date, not null.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null`.
    :   `ClassCastException` - if the object type is not a [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") or [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util").
    :   `ArithmeticException` - if the year is over 280 million.

    Since:

    public static long [getFragmentInDays](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-509)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar,
    int fragment)

    Gets the number of days within the
    fragment. All datefields greater than the fragment will be ignored.

    Asking the days of any date will only return the number of days
    of the current month (resulting in a number between 1 and 31). This
    method will retrieve the number of days for any fragment.
    For example, if you want to calculate the number of days past this year,
    your fragment is Calendar.YEAR. The result will be all days of the
    past month(s).

    Valid fragments are: Calendar.YEAR, Calendar.MONTH, both
    Calendar.DAY\_OF\_YEAR and Calendar.DATE, Calendar.HOUR\_OF\_DAY,
    Calendar.MINUTE, Calendar.SECOND and Calendar.MILLISECOND
    A fragment less than or equal to a DAY field will return 0.

    * January 28, 2008 with Calendar.MONTH as fragment will return 28
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.DAY\_OF\_MONTH))
    * February 28, 2008 with Calendar.MONTH as fragment will return 28
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.DAY\_OF\_MONTH))
    * January 28, 2008 with Calendar.YEAR as fragment will return 28
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.DAY\_OF\_YEAR))
    * February 28, 2008 with Calendar.YEAR as fragment will return 59
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.DAY\_OF\_YEAR))
    * January 28, 2008 with Calendar.MILLISECOND as fragment will return 0
      (a millisecond cannot be split in days)

    Parameters:
    :   `calendar` - the calendar to work with, not null.
    :   `fragment` - the [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") field part of calendar to calculate.

    Returns:
    :   number of days within the fragment of date.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null` or
        fragment is not supported.

    Since:
    :   2.4

    public static long [getFragmentInMilliseconds](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-661)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar,
    int fragment)

    Gets the number of milliseconds within the
    fragment. All date fields greater than the fragment will be ignored.

    Asking the milliseconds of any date will only return the number of milliseconds
    of the current second (resulting in a number between 0 and 999). This
    method will retrieve the number of milliseconds for any fragment.
    For example, if you want to calculate the number of seconds past today,
    your fragment is Calendar.DATE or Calendar.DAY\_OF\_YEAR. The result will
    be all seconds of the past hour(s), minutes(s) and second(s).

    Valid fragments are: Calendar.YEAR, Calendar.MONTH, both
    Calendar.DAY\_OF\_YEAR and Calendar.DATE, Calendar.HOUR\_OF\_DAY,
    Calendar.MINUTE, Calendar.SECOND and Calendar.MILLISECOND
    A fragment less than or equal to a MILLISECOND field will return 0.

    * January 1, 2008 7:15:10.538 with Calendar.SECOND as fragment will return 538
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.MILLISECOND))
    * January 6, 2008 7:15:10.538 with Calendar.SECOND as fragment will return 538
      (equivalent to calendar.get(Calendar.MILLISECOND))
    * January 6, 2008 7:15:10.538 with Calendar.MINUTE as fragment will return 10538
      (10\*1000 + 538)
    * January 16, 2008 7:15:10.538 with Calendar.MILLISECOND as fragment will return 0
      (a millisecond cannot be split in milliseconds)

    Parameters:
    :   `calendar` - the calendar to work with, not null.
    :   `fragment` - the [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") field part of calendar to calculate.

    Returns:
    :   number of milliseconds within the fragment of date.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null` or
        fragment is not supported.

    Since:
    :   2.4

  * ### iterator

    public static [Iterator](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util")<[Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util")> [iterator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-973)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar,
    int rangeStyle)

    Constructs an [`Iterator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util") over each day in a date
    range defined by a focus date and range style.

    For instance, passing Thursday, July 4, 2002 and a
    `RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY` will return an [`Iterator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util")
    that starts with Sunday, June 30, 2002 and ends with Saturday, August 3,
    2002, returning a Calendar instance for each intermediate day.

    This method provides an iterator that returns Calendar objects.
    The days are progressed using [`Calendar.add(int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html#add-int-int- "class or interface in java.util").

    Parameters:
    :   `calendar` - the date to work with, not null.
    :   `rangeStyle` - the style constant to use. Must be one of
        [`RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY`](#RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY),
        [`RANGE_MONTH_MONDAY`](#RANGE_MONTH_MONDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_SUNDAY`](#RANGE_WEEK_SUNDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_MONDAY`](#RANGE_WEEK_MONDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_RELATIVE`](#RANGE_WEEK_RELATIVE),

  * ### iterator

    public static [Iterator](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util")<[Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util")> [iterator](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-1069)([Date](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") focus,
    int rangeStyle)

    Constructs an [`Iterator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util") over each day in a date
    range defined by a focus date and range style.

    For instance, passing Thursday, July 4, 2002 and a
    `RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY` will return an [`Iterator`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Iterator.html "class or interface in java.util")
    that starts with Sunday, June 30, 2002 and ends with Saturday, August 3,
    2002, returning a Calendar instance for each intermediate day.

    This method provides an iterator that returns Calendar objects.
    The days are progressed using [`Calendar.add(int, int)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html#add-int-int- "class or interface in java.util").

    Parameters:
    :   `focus` - the date to work with, not null.
    :   `rangeStyle` - the style constant to use. Must be one of
        [`RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY`](#RANGE_MONTH_SUNDAY),
        [`RANGE_MONTH_MONDAY`](#RANGE_MONTH_MONDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_SUNDAY`](#RANGE_WEEK_SUNDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_MONDAY`](#RANGE_WEEK_MONDAY),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_RELATIVE`](#RANGE_WEEK_RELATIVE),
        [`RANGE_WEEK_CENTER`](#RANGE_WEEK_CENTER).

    Returns:
    :   the date iterator, not null, not null.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null`.
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the rangeStyle is invalid.

  * ### parseDate

    public static [Date](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") [parseDate](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-1259)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") str,
    [Locale](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Locale.html "class or interface in java.util") locale,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")... parsePatterns)
    throws [ParseException](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/ParseException.html "class or interface in java.text")

    Parses a string representing a date by trying a variety of different parsers,
    using the default date format symbols for the given locale.

    The parse will try each parse pattern in turn.
    A parse is only deemed successful if it parses the whole of the input string.
    If no parse patterns match, a ParseException is thrown.

    The parser will be lenient toward the parsed date.

    Parameters:
    :   `str` - the date to parse, not null.
    :   `locale` - the locale whose date format symbols should be used. If `null`,
        the system locale is used (as per [`parseDate(String, String...)`](#parseDate(java.lang.String,java.lang.String...))).
    :   `parsePatterns` - the date format patterns to use, see SimpleDateFormat, not null.

    Returns:
    :   the parsed date.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date string or pattern array is null.
    :   `ParseException` - if none of the date patterns were suitable (or there were none).

    Since:
    :   3.2

    Parses a string representing a date by trying a variety of different parsers,
    using the default date format symbols for the given locale.

    The parse will try each parse pattern in turn.
    A parse is only deemed successful if it parses the whole of the input string.

    The parser parses strictly - it does not allow for dates such as "February 942, 1996".

    :   `parsePatterns` - the date format patterns to use, see SimpleDateFormat, not null.

  * ### round

    public static [Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") [round](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-1392)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar,
    int field)

    Rounds a date, leaving the field specified as the most
    significant field.

    For example, if you had the date-time of 28 Mar 2002
    13:45:01.231, if this was passed with HOUR, it would return
    28 Mar 2002 14:00:00.000. If this was passed with MONTH, it
    would return 1 April 2002 0:00:00.000.

    For a date in a time zone that handles the change to daylight
    saving time, rounding to Calendar.HOUR\_OF\_DAY will behave as follows.
    Suppose daylight saving time begins at 02:00 on March 30. Rounding a
    date that crosses this time would produce the following values:

    * March 30, 2003 01:10 rounds to March 30, 2003 01:00
    * March 30, 2003 01:40 rounds to March 30, 2003 03:00
    * March 30, 2003 02:10 rounds to March 30, 2003 03:00
    * March 30, 2003 02:40 rounds to March 30, 2003 04:00

    Parameters:
    :   `calendar` - the date to work with, not null.
    :   `field` - the field from [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") or `SEMI_MONTH`.

    Returns:
    :   the different rounded date, not null.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null`.
    :   `ArithmeticException` - if the year is over 280 million.

  * ### truncate

    public static [Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") [truncate](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtils.html#line-1716)([Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") date,
    int field)

    Truncates a date, leaving the field specified as the most
    significant field.

    For example, if you had the date-time of 28 Mar 2002
    13:45:01.231, if you passed with HOUR, it would return 28 Mar
    2002 13:00:00.000. If this was passed with MONTH, it would
    return 1 Mar 2002 0:00:00.000.

    Parameters:
    :   `date` - the date to work with, not null.
    :   `field` - the field from [`Calendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") or `SEMI_MONTH`.

    Returns:
    :   the different truncated date, not null.

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the date is `null`.
    :   `ArithmeticException` - if the year is over 280 million.

Package [org.apache.commons.lang3](package-summary.html)

# Class RandomUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.RandomUtils

---

public class [RandomUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/RandomUtils.html#line-71)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Supplements the standard [`Random`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Random.html "class or interface in java.util") class.

Use [`secure()`](#secure()) to get the singleton instance based on [`SecureRandom()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/SecureRandom.html#-init--- "class or interface in java.security") which uses a secure random number generator implementing the
default random number algorithm.

Use [`secureStrong()`](#secureStrong()) to get the singleton instance based on [`SecureRandom.getInstanceStrong()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/SecureRandom.html#getInstanceStrong-- "class or interface in java.security") which uses an instance that was selected by using
the algorithms/providers specified in the `securerandom.strongAlgorithms` [`Security`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/Security.html "class or interface in java.security") property.

Use [`insecure()`](#insecure()) to get the singleton instance based on [`ThreadLocalRandom.current()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/ThreadLocalRandom.html#current-- "class or interface in java.util.concurrent") **which is not cryptographically secure**. In addition,
instances do not use a cryptographically random seed unless the [system property](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/System.html#getProperty-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.lang") `java.util.secureRandomSeed` is set to
`true`.

Starting in version 3.17.0, the method [`secure()`](#secure()) uses [`SecureRandom()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/SecureRandom.html#-init--- "class or interface in java.security") instead of [`SecureRandom.getInstanceStrong()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/SecureRandom.html#getInstanceStrong-- "class or interface in java.security"), and
adds [`secureStrong()`](#secureStrong()).

Starting in version 3.16.0, this class uses [`secure()`](#secure()) for static methods and adds [`insecure()`](#insecure()).

Starting in version 3.15.0, this class uses [`SecureRandom.getInstanceStrong()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/security/SecureRandom.html#getInstanceStrong-- "class or interface in java.security") for static methods.

Before version 3.15.0, this class used [`ThreadLocalRandom.current()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/ThreadLocalRandom.html#current-- "class or interface in java.util.concurrent") for static methods, which is not cryptographically secure.

Please note that the Apache Commons project provides a component dedicated to pseudo-random number generation, namely
[Commons RNG](https://commons.apache.org/proper/commons-rng/), that may be a better choice for applications with more stringent requirements
(performance and/or correctness).

Since:
:   3.3

See Also:
:   * [`secure()`](#secure())

Package [org.apache.commons.lang3.builder](package-summary.html)

# Class ReflectionDiffBuilder<T>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ReflectionDiffBuilder<T>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - type of the left and right object to diff.

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Builder<DiffResult<T>>`

---

public class [ReflectionDiffBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ReflectionDiffBuilder.html#line-78)<T>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Builder](Builder.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<[DiffResult](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<T>>

Assists in implementing [`Diffable.diff(Object)`](Diffable.html#diff(T)) methods.

All non-static, non-transient fields (including inherited fields) of the objects to diff are discovered using reflection and compared for differences.

To use this class, write code as follows:

```
 public class Person implements Diffable<Person> {
   String name;
   int age;
   boolean smoker;
   ...

   public DiffResult<Person> diff(Person obj) {
     // No need for null check, as NullPointerException correct if obj is null
     return ReflectionDiffBuilder.<Person>builder()
       .setDiffBuilder(DiffBuilder.<Person>builder()
           .setLeft(this)
           .setRight(obj)
           .setStyle(ToStringStyle.SHORT_PREFIX_STYLE)
           .build())
       .setExcludeFieldNames("userName", "password")
       .build()  // -> ReflectionDiffBuilder
       .build(); // -> DiffResult
   }
 }
```

The [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") passed to the constructor is embedded in the returned [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") and influences the style of the
`DiffResult.toString()` method. This style choice can be overridden by calling [`DiffResult.toString(ToStringStyle)`](DiffResult.html#toString(org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle)).

See [`DiffBuilder`](DiffBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") for a non-reflection based version of this class.

Since:
:   3.6

See Also:
:   * [`Diffable`](Diffable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

* ## Constructor Details

  * ### ReflectionDiffBuilder

    [@Deprecated](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Deprecated.html "class or interface in java.lang")
    public [ReflectionDiffBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ReflectionDiffBuilder.html#line-183)([T](ReflectionDiffBuilder.html "type parameter in ReflectionDiffBuilder") left,
    [T](ReflectionDiffBuilder.html "type parameter in ReflectionDiffBuilder") right,
    [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") style)

    Deprecated.

    Use [`ReflectionDiffBuilder.Builder`](ReflectionDiffBuilder.Builder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder").

    Constructs a builder for the specified objects with the specified style.

    If `left == right` or `left.equals(right)` then the builder will not evaluate any calls to `append(...)` and will return an empty
    [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") when [`build()`](#build()) is executed.

    Parameters:
    :   `left` - `this` object.
    :   `right` - the object to diff against.
    :   `style` - the style will use when outputting the objects, `null` uses the default

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if `left` or `right` is `null`.

public class [MutableByte](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/mutable/MutableByte.html#line-34)
extends [Number](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Number.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Comparable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Comparable.html "class or interface in java.lang")<[MutableByte](MutableByte.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.mutable")>, [Mutable](Mutable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.mutable")<[Number](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Number.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

A mutable `byte` wrapper.

This class was created before the introduction of the [`java.util.concurrent.atomic`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/atomic/package-summary.html) package and the [`AtomicInteger`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/concurrent/atomic/AtomicInteger.html "class or interface in java.util.concurrent.atomic") class.

Note that as MutableByte does not extend Byte, it is not treated by String.format as a Byte parameter.

Since:
:   2.1

* ## Method Details

  * ### inContainer

    public static [Boolean](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html "class or interface in java.lang") [inContainer](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/RuntimeEnvironment.html#line-68)()

    Tests whether we are running in a container like Docker or Podman.

    *The following may change if we find better detection logic.*

    We roughly follow the logic in SystemD:

    <https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/0747e3b60eb4496ee122066c844210ce818d76d9/src/basic/virt.c#L692>

    We check the `container` environment variable of process 1:

    1. If the variable is empty, we return false. This includes the case, where the container developer wants to hide the fact that the application runs in
       a container.
    2. If the variable is not empty, we return true.
    3. If the variable is absent, we continue.
    4. We check files in the container. According to SystemD:/
       1. /.dockerenv is used by Docker.
       2. /run/.containerenv is used by PodMan.

    Returns:
    :   whether we are running in a container like Docker or Podman. Never null.

    See Also:
    :   * [SystemD virt.c](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/blob/0747e3b60eb4496ee122066c844210ce818d76d9/src/basic/virt.c#L692)

---

public class [DateFormatUtils](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateFormatUtils.html#line-39)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Date and time formatting utilities and constants.

Formatting is performed using the thread-safe
[`FastDateFormat`](FastDateFormat.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.time") class.

Note that the JDK has a bug wherein calling Calendar.get(int) will
override any previously called Calendar.clear() calls. See LANG-755.

Note that when using capital YYYY instead of lowercase yyyy, the formatter
will assume current year as week year is not supported. See [`GregorianCalendar`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/GregorianCalendar.html "class or interface in java.util")
Week Year section for an explanation on the difference between calendar and week years.

Since:
:   2.0

    ISO 8601-like formatter for date with time zone.

    The format used is `yyyy-MM-ddZZ`. This pattern does not comply

    effect at the time of loading DateFormatUtils class.

# Class AnnotationUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.AnnotationUtils

---

public class [AnnotationUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/AnnotationUtils.html#line-45)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Helper methods for working with [`Annotation`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html "class or interface in java.lang.annotation") instances.

This class contains various utility methods that make working with
annotations simpler.

[`Annotation`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html "class or interface in java.lang.annotation") instances are always proxy objects; unfortunately
dynamic proxies cannot be depended upon to know how to implement certain
methods in the same manner as would be done by "natural" [`Annotation`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html "class or interface in java.lang.annotation")s.
The methods presented in this class can be used to avoid that possibility. It
is of course also possible for dynamic proxies to actually delegate their
e.g. [`Annotation.equals(Object)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html#equals-java.lang.Object- "class or interface in java.lang.annotation")/[`Annotation.hashCode()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html#hashCode-- "class or interface in java.lang.annotation")/
[`Annotation.toString()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html#toString-- "class or interface in java.lang.annotation") implementations to [`AnnotationUtils`](AnnotationUtils.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3").

#ThreadSafe#

  * ### isValidAnnotationMemberType

    public static boolean [isValidAnnotationMemberType](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/AnnotationUtils.html#line-287)([Class](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?> type)

    Checks if the specified type is permitted as an annotation member.

    The Java language specification only permits certain types to be used
    in annotations. These include [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang"), [`Class`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang"), primitive
    types, [`Annotation`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/annotation/Annotation.html "class or interface in java.lang.annotation"), [`Enum`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Enum.html "class or interface in java.lang"), and single-dimensional arrays of
    these types.

    Parameters:
    :   `type` - the type to check, `null`

    Returns:
    :   `true` if the type is a valid type to use in an annotation

# Class ClassUtils

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.ClassUtils

---

public class [ClassUtils](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/ClassUtils.html#line-51)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Operates on classes without using reflection.

This class handles invalid `null` inputs as best it can. Each method documents its behavior in more detail.

The notion of a `canonical name` includes the human-readable name for the type, for example `int[]`. The
non-canonical method variants work with the JVM names, such as `[I`.

    Given a [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util") of [`Class`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang") objects, this method converts them into class names.

    Returns:

  * ### convertClassNamesToClasses

    public static [List](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util")<[Class](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?>> [convertClassNamesToClasses](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/ClassUtils.html#line-223)([List](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")> classNames)

    Given a [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util") of class names, this method converts them into classes.

    A new [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util") is returned. If the class name cannot be found, `null` is stored in the [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util"). If the
    class name in the [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util") is `null`, `null` is stored in the output [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util").

    Parameters:
    :   `classNames` - the classNames to change.

    Returns:
    :   a [`List`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util") of Class objects corresponding to the class names, `null` if null input.

    Throws:
    :   `ClassCastException` - if classNames contains a non String entry.
