* ## Method Details

  * ### toString

    public static [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [toString](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ReflectionToStringBuilder.html#line-155)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") object)

    Builds a `toString` value using the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") through reflection.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private fields. This means that it will
    throw a security exception if run under a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is
    also not as efficient as testing explicitly.

    Transient members will be not be included, as they are likely derived. Static fields will not be included.
    Superclass fields will be appended.

    Parameters:
    :   `object` - the Object to be output

    Returns:
    :   the String result

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the Object is `null`

    See Also:
    :   * [`ToStringExclude`](ToStringExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")
        * [`ToStringSummary`](ToStringSummary.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

    Builds a `toString` value through reflection.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private fields. This means that it will
    throw a security exception if run under a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is
    also not as efficient as testing explicitly.

    If the `outputTransients` is `true`, transient members will be output, otherwise they
    are ignored, as they are likely derived fields, and not part of the value of the Object.

    Static fields will not be included. Superclass fields will be appended.

    If the style is `null`, the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") is used.

# Class HashCodeBuilder

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.HashCodeBuilder

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Builder<Integer>`

---

public class [HashCodeBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/HashCodeBuilder.html#line-105)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Builder](Builder.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<[Integer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Integer.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

Assists in implementing [`Object.hashCode()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html#hashCode-- "class or interface in java.lang") methods.

This class enables a good `hashCode` method to be built for any class. It follows the rules laid out in
the book [Effective Java](https://www.oracle.com/technetwork/java/effectivejava-136174.html) by Joshua Bloch. Writing a
good `hashCode` method is actually quite difficult. This class aims to simplify the process.

The following is the approach taken. When appending a data field, the current total is multiplied by the
multiplier then a relevant value
for that data type is added. For example, if the current hashCode is 17, and the multiplier is 37, then
appending the integer 45 will create a hash code of 674, namely 17 \* 37 + 45.

All relevant fields from the object should be included in the `hashCode` method. Derived fields may be
excluded. In general, any field used in the `equals` method must be used in the `hashCode`
method.

To use this class write code as follows:

```
 public class Person {
   String name;
   int age;
   boolean smoker;
   ...

   public int hashCode() {
     // you pick a hard-coded, randomly chosen, non-zero, odd number
     // ideally different for each class
     return new HashCodeBuilder(17, 37).
       append(name).
       append(age).
       append(smoker).
       toHashCode();
   }
 }
```

If required, the superclass `hashCode()` can be added using [`appendSuper(int)`](#appendSuper(int)).

Alternatively, there is a method that uses reflection to determine the fields to test. Because these fields are
usually private, the method, `reflectionHashCode`, uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible`
to change the visibility of the fields. This will fail under a security manager, unless the appropriate permissions
are set up correctly. It is also slower than testing explicitly.

A typical invocation for this method would look like:

```
 public int hashCode() {
   return HashCodeBuilder.reflectionHashCode(this);
 }
```

The [`HashCodeExclude`](HashCodeExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") annotation can be used to exclude fields from being
used by the `reflectionHashCode` methods.

    Two randomly chosen, odd numbers must be passed in. Ideally these should be different for each class,
    however this is not vital.

    Prime numbers are preferred, especially for the multiplier.

    Parameters:

* ## Method Details

  * ### reflectionHashCode

    public static int [reflectionHashCode](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/HashCodeBuilder.html#line-241)(int initialNonZeroOddNumber,
    int multiplierNonZeroOddNumber,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") object)

    Uses reflection to build a valid hash code from the fields of `object`.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private fields. This means that it will
    throw a security exception if run under a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is
    also not as efficient as testing explicitly.

    Transient members will be not be used, as they are likely derived fields, and not part of the value of the
    [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Static fields will not be tested. Superclass fields will be included.

    Two randomly chosen, non-zero, odd numbers must be passed in. Ideally these should be different for each class,
    however this is not vital. Prime numbers are preferred, especially for the multiplier.

    Parameters:
    :   `initialNonZeroOddNumber` - a non-zero, odd number used as the initial value. This will be the returned
        value if no fields are found to include in the hash code
    :   `multiplierNonZeroOddNumber` - a non-zero, odd number used as the multiplier
    :   `object` - the Object to create a `hashCode` for

    Returns:
    :   int hash code

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the Object is `null`
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - if the number is zero or even

    See Also:
    :   * [`HashCodeExclude`](HashCodeExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

    Returns:

    public static int [reflectionHashCode](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/HashCodeBuilder.html#line-384)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") object,
    boolean testTransients)

    Uses reflection to build a valid hash code from the fields of `object`.

    This constructor uses two hard coded choices for the constants needed to build a hash code.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private fields. This means that it will
    throw a security exception if run under a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is
    also not as efficient as testing explicitly.

    If the TestTransients parameter is set to `true`, transient members will be tested, otherwise they
    are ignored, as they are likely derived fields, and not part of the value of the [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Static fields will not be tested. Superclass fields will be included. If no fields are found to include
    in the hash code, the result of this method will be constant.

    Parameters:
    :   `object` - the Object to create a `hashCode` for
    :   `testTransients` - whether to include transient fields

    Returns:
    :   int hash code

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the object is `null`

    See Also:
    :   * [`HashCodeExclude`](HashCodeExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

  * ### append

    public [HashCodeBuilder](HashCodeBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [append](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/HashCodeBuilder.html#line-553)(boolean value)

    Append a `hashCode` for a `boolean`.

    This adds `1` when true, and `0` when false to the `hashCode`.

    This is in contrast to the standard [`Boolean.hashCode()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html#hashCode-- "class or interface in java.lang") handling, which computes
    a `hashCode` value of `1231` for [`Boolean`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html "class or interface in java.lang") instances
    that represent `true` or `1237` for [`Boolean`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html "class or interface in java.lang") instances
    that represent `false`.

    This is in accordance with the *Effective Java* design.

    Parameters:
    :   `value` - the boolean to add to the `hashCode`

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

Package [org.apache.commons.lang3.builder](package-summary.html)

# Class ToStringBuilder

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringBuilder

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Builder<String>`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `ReflectionToStringBuilder`

---

public class [ToStringBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-90)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Builder](Builder.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<[String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

Assists in implementing [`Object.toString()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html#toString-- "class or interface in java.lang") methods.

This class enables a good and consistent `toString()` to be built for any
class or object. This class aims to simplify the process by:

* allowing field names
* handling all types consistently
* handling nulls consistently
* outputting arrays and multi-dimensional arrays
* enabling the detail level to be controlled for Objects and Collections
* handling class hierarchies

To use this class write code as follows:

```
 public class Person {
   String name;
   int age;
   boolean smoker;

   ...

   public String toString() {
     return new ToStringBuilder(this).
       append("name", name).
       append("age", age).
       append("smoker", smoker).
       toString();
   }
 }
```

This will produce a toString of the format:
`Person@7f54[name=Stephen,age=29,smoker=false]`

To add the superclass `toString`, use [`appendSuper(java.lang.String)`](#appendSuper(java.lang.String)).
To append the `toString` from an object that is delegated
to (or any other object), use [`appendToString(java.lang.String)`](#appendToString(java.lang.String)).

Alternatively, there is a method that uses reflection to determine
the fields to test. Because these fields are usually private, the method,
`reflectionToString`, uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to
change the visibility of the fields. This will fail under a security manager,
unless the appropriate permissions are set up correctly. It is also
slower than testing explicitly.

A typical invocation for this method would look like:

```
 public String toString() {
   return ToStringBuilder.reflectionToString(this);
 }
```

You can also use the builder to debug 3rd party objects:

```
 System.out.println("An object: " + ToStringBuilder.reflectionToString(anObject));
```

The exact format of the `toString` is determined by
the [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") passed into the constructor.

Since:
:   1.0

    public [ToStringBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-220)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") object)

* ## Method Details

  * ### getDefaultStyle

    public static [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [getDefaultStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-115)()

    Gets the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to use.

    This method gets a singleton default value, typically for the whole JVM.
    Changing this default should generally only be done during application startup.
    It is recommended to pass a [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to the constructor instead
    of using this global default.

    This method can be used from multiple threads.
    Internally, a `volatile` variable is used to provide the guarantee
    that the latest value set using [`setDefaultStyle(org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle)`](#setDefaultStyle(org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle)) is the value returned.
    It is strongly recommended that the default style is only changed during application startup.

    One reason for changing the default could be to have a verbose style during
    development and a compact style in production.

    Returns:
    :   the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), never null

  * ### setDefaultStyle

    public static void [setDefaultStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-194)([ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") style)

    Sets the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to use.

    This method sets a singleton default value, typically for the whole JVM.
    Changing this default should generally only be done during application startup.
    It is recommended to pass a [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to the constructor instead
    of changing this global default.

    This method is not intended for use from multiple threads.
    Internally, a `volatile` variable is used to provide the guarantee
    that the latest value set is the value returned from [`getDefaultStyle()`](#getDefaultStyle()).

    Parameters:
    :   `style` - the default [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if the style is `null`

    public [ToStringBuilder](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [append](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-518)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") fieldName,
    boolean[] array,
    boolean fullDetail)

    Append to the `toString` a `boolean`
    array.

    A boolean parameter controls the level of detail to show.
    Setting `true` will output the array in full. Setting
    `false` will output a summary, typically the size of
    the array.

    Parameters:
    :   `fieldName` - the field name
    :   `array` - the array to add to the `toString`
    :   `fullDetail` - `true` for detail, `false`
        for summary info

  * ### appendToString

    public [ToStringBuilder](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [appendToString](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringBuilder.html#line-966)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") toString)

    Append the `toString` from another object.

    This method is useful where a class delegates most of the implementation of
    its properties to another class. You can then call `toString()` on
    the other class and pass the result into this method.

    ```
       private AnotherObject delegate;
       private String fieldInThisClass;

       public String toString() {
         return new ToStringBuilder(this).
           appendToString(delegate.toString()).
           append(fieldInThisClass).
           toString();
       }
    ```

    This method assumes that the other object uses the same [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")
    as this one.

    If the `toString` is `null`, no change is made.

    Parameters:
    :   `toString` - the result of `toString()` on another object

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

    Since:
    :   2.0

# Class MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

[org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.RecursiveToStringStyle](RecursiveToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`

---

public class [MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle.html#line-65)
extends [RecursiveToStringStyle](RecursiveToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

Works with [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to create a "deep" `toString`.
But instead a single line like the [`RecursiveToStringStyle`](RecursiveToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") this creates a multiline String
similar to the [`ToStringStyle.MULTI_LINE_STYLE`](ToStringStyle.html#MULTI_LINE_STYLE).

To use this class write code as follows:

```
 public class Job {
   String title;
   ...
 }

 public class Person {
   String name;
   int age;
   boolean smoker;
   Job job;

   ...

   public String toString() {
     return new ReflectionToStringBuilder(this, new MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle()).toString();
   }
 }
```

This will produce a toString of the format:  
`Person@7f54[ <br>
&nbsp; name=Stephen, <br>
&nbsp; age=29, <br>
&nbsp; smokealse, <br>
&nbsp; job=Job@43cd2[ <br>
&nbsp; &nbsp; title=Manager <br>
&nbsp; ] <br>
]`

Since:
:   3.4

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle)

# Class EqualsBuilder

public class [EqualsBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/EqualsBuilder.html#line-89)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Builder](Builder.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<[Boolean](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Boolean.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

Assists in implementing [`Object.equals(Object)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html#equals-java.lang.Object- "class or interface in java.lang") methods.

This class provides methods to build a good equals method for any
class. It follows rules laid out in
[Effective Java](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/effectivejava.html)
, by Joshua Bloch. In particular the rule for comparing `doubles`,
`floats`, and arrays can be tricky. Also, making sure that
`equals()` and `hashCode()` are consistent can be
difficult.

Two Objects that compare as equals must generate the same hash code,
but two Objects with the same hash code do not have to be equal.

All relevant fields should be included in the calculation of equals.
Derived fields may be ignored. In particular, any field used in
generating a hash code must be used in the equals method, and vice
versa.

Typical use for the code is as follows:

```
 public boolean equals(Object obj) {
   if (obj == null) { return false; }
   if (obj == this) { return true; }
   if (obj.getClass() != getClass()) {
     return false;
   }
   MyClass rhs = (MyClass) obj;
   return new EqualsBuilder()
                 .appendSuper(super.equals(obj))
                 .append(field1, rhs.field1)
                 .append(field2, rhs.field2)
                 .append(field3, rhs.field3)
                 .isEquals();
  }
```

Alternatively, there is a method that uses reflection to determine
the fields to test. Because these fields are usually private, the method,
`reflectionEquals`, uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to
change the visibility of the fields. This will fail under a security
manager, unless the appropriate permissions are set up correctly. It is
also slower than testing explicitly. Non-primitive fields are compared using
`equals()`.

A typical invocation for this method would look like:

```
 public boolean equals(Object obj) {
   return EqualsBuilder.reflectionEquals(this, obj);
 }
```

The [`EqualsExclude`](EqualsExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") annotation can be used to exclude fields from being
used by the `reflectionEquals` methods.

    This method uses reflection to determine if the two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s
    are equal.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private
    fields. This means that it will throw a security exception if run under
    a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is also
    not as efficient as testing explicitly. Non-primitive fields are compared using
    `equals()`.

    If the TestTransients parameter is set to `true`, transient
    members will be tested, otherwise they are ignored, as they are likely
    derived fields, and not part of the value of the [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Static fields will not be tested. Superclass fields will be included.

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - `this` object
    :   `rhs` - the other object
    :   `testTransients` - whether to include transient fields

    Returns:
    :   `true` if the two Objects have tested equals.

    See Also:
    :   * [`EqualsExclude`](EqualsExclude.html "annotation in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

    public static boolean [reflectionEquals](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/EqualsBuilder.html#line-218)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") lhs,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") rhs,
    boolean testTransients,
    [Class](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?> reflectUpToClass,
    boolean testRecursive,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")... excludeFields)

    This method uses reflection to determine if the two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s
    are equal.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private
    fields. This means that it will throw a security exception if run under
    a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is also
    not as efficient as testing explicitly. Non-primitive fields are compared using
    `equals()`.

    If the testTransients parameter is set to `true`, transient
    members will be tested, otherwise they are ignored, as they are likely
    derived fields, and not part of the value of the [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Static fields will not be included. Superclass fields will be appended
    up to and including the specified superclass. A null superclass is treated
    as java.lang.Object.

    If the testRecursive parameter is set to `true`, non primitive
    (and non primitive wrapper) field types will be compared by
    [`EqualsBuilder`](EqualsBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") recursively instead of invoking their
    `equals()` method. Leading to a deep reflection equals test.

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - `this` object
    :   `rhs` - the other object
    :   `testTransients` - whether to include transient fields
    :   `reflectUpToClass` - the superclass to reflect up to (inclusive),
        may be `null`
    :   `testRecursive` - whether to call reflection equals on non-primitive
        fields recursively.
    :   `excludeFields` - array of field names to exclude from testing

    Returns:
    :   `true` if the two Objects have tested equals.

    Since:
    :   3.6

  * ### reflectionAppend

    public [EqualsBuilder](EqualsBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [reflectionAppend](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/EqualsBuilder.html#line-924)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") lhs,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") rhs)

    Tests if two `objects` by using reflection.

    It uses `AccessibleObject.setAccessible` to gain access to private
    fields. This means that it will throw a security exception if run under
    a security manager, if the permissions are not set up correctly. It is also
    not as efficient as testing explicitly. Non-primitive fields are compared using
    `equals()`.

    If the testTransients field is set to `true`, transient
    members will be tested, otherwise they are ignored, as they are likely
    derived fields, and not part of the value of the [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang").

    Static fields will not be included. Superclass fields will be appended
    up to and including the specified superclass in field `reflectUpToClass`.
    A null superclass is treated as java.lang.Object.

    Field names listed in field `excludeFields` will be ignored.

    If either class of the compared objects is contained in
    `bypassReflectionClasses`, both objects are compared by calling
    the equals method of the left-hand side object with the right-hand side object as an argument.

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - the left-hand side object
    :   `rhs` - the right-hand side object

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

  * ### setBypassReflectionClasses

    public [EqualsBuilder](EqualsBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [setBypassReflectionClasses](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/EqualsBuilder.html#line-1045)([List](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/List.html "class or interface in java.util")<[Class](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?>> bypassReflectionClasses)

    Sets [`Class`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")es whose instances should be compared by calling their `equals`
    although being in recursive mode. So the fields of these classes will not be compared recursively by reflection.

    Here you should name classes having non-transient fields which are cache fields being set lazily.  
    Prominent example being [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") class with its hash code cache field. Due to the importance
    of the [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") class, it is included in the default bypasses classes. Usually, if you use
    your own set of classes here, remember to include [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") class, too.

    Parameters:
    :   `bypassReflectionClasses` - classes to bypass reflection test

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

    Since:
    :   3.8

    See Also:
    :   * [`setTestRecursive(boolean)`](#setTestRecursive(boolean))

    Sets whether to test fields recursively, instead of using their equals method, when reflectively comparing objects.

# Class StandardToStringStyle

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.StandardToStringStyle

---

public class [StandardToStringStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/StandardToStringStyle.html#line-34)
extends [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

Works with [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to create a `toString`.

This class is intended to be used as a singleton.
There is no need to instantiate a new style each time.
Simply instantiate the class once, customize the values as required, and
store the result in a public static final variable for the rest of the
program to access.

Since:
:   1.0

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.StandardToStringStyle)

# Class DiffResult<T>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

public class [DiffResult](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/DiffResult.html#line-39)<T>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Iterable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html "class or interface in java.lang")<[Diff](Diff.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<?>>

A [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") contains a collection of the differences between two
[`Diffable`](Diffable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") objects. Typically these differences are displayed using
[`toString()`](#toString()) method, which returns a string describing the fields that
differ between the objects.

Use a [`DiffBuilder`](DiffBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to build a [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") comparing two objects.

Since:
:   3.3

  * ### toString

    public [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") [toString](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/DiffResult.html#line-166)()

    Builds a [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") description of the differences contained within
    this [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"). A [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") is used for each object
    and the style of the output is governed by the [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")
    passed to the constructor.

    If there are no differences stored in this list, the method will return
    [`OBJECTS_SAME_STRING`](#OBJECTS_SAME_STRING). Otherwise, using the example given in
    [`Diffable`](Diffable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") and [`ToStringStyle.SHORT_PREFIX_STYLE`](ToStringStyle.html#SHORT_PREFIX_STYLE), an output
    might be:

    ```
     Person[name=John Doe,age=32] differs from Person[name=Joe Bloggs,age=26]
    ```

    This indicates that the objects differ in name and age, but not in
    smoking status.

    To use a different [`ToStringStyle`](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") for an instance of this class,
    use [`toString(ToStringStyle)`](#toString(org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle)).

    Overrides:
    :   `toString` in class `Object`

    Returns:
    :   a [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") description of the differences.

# Class ToStringStyle

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `RecursiveToStringStyle`, `StandardToStringStyle`

---

public abstract class [ToStringStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-69)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

Controls [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") formatting for [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"). The main public interface is always via [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder").

These classes are intended to be used as *singletons*. There is no need to instantiate a new style each time. A program will generally use one of the
predefined constants on this class. Alternatively, the [`StandardToStringStyle`](StandardToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") class can be used to set the individual settings. Thus most styles can
be achieved without subclassing.

If required, a subclass can override as many or as few of the methods as it requires. Each object type (from `boolean` to `long` to
[`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") to `int[]`) has its own methods to output it. Most have two versions, detail and summary.

For example, the detail version of the array based methods will output the whole array, whereas the summary method will just output the array length.

If you want to format the output of certain objects, such as dates, you must create a subclass and override a method.

```
 public class MyStyle extends ToStringStyle {

     protected void appendDetail(StringBuffer buffer, String fieldName, Object value) {
         if (value instanceof Date) {
             value = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd").format(value);
         }
         buffer.append(value);
     }
 }
```

Since:
:   1.0

See Also:
:   * [Serialized Form](../../../../../serialized-form.html#org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle)

* ## Field Details

  * ### DEFAULT\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [DEFAULT\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-507)

    The default toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     Person@182f0db[name=John Doe,age=33,smoker=false]
    ```
  * ### MULTI\_LINE\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [MULTI\_LINE\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-520)

    The multi line toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     Person@182f0db[
       name=John Doe
       age=33
       smoker=false
     ]
    ```
  * ### NO\_FIELD\_NAMES\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [NO\_FIELD\_NAMES\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-529)

    The no field names toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     Person@182f0db[John Doe,33,false]
    ```
  * ### SHORT\_PREFIX\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [SHORT\_PREFIX\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-540)

    The short prefix toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     Person[name=John Doe,age=33,smoker=false]
    ```

    Since:
    :   2.1
  * ### SIMPLE\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [SIMPLE\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-549)

    The simple toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     John Doe,33,false
    ```
  * ### NO\_CLASS\_NAME\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [NO\_CLASS\_NAME\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-560)

    The no class name toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     [name=John Doe,age=33,smoker=false]
    ```

    Since:
    :   3.4
  * ### JSON\_STYLE

    public static final [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [JSON\_STYLE](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-576)

    The JSON toString style. Using the `Person` example from [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder"), the output would look like this:

    ```
     {"name": "John Doe", "age": 33, "smoker": true}
    ```

    **Note:** Since field names are mandatory in JSON, this ToStringStyle will throw an [`UnsupportedOperationException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/UnsupportedOperationException.html "class or interface in java.lang") if no field name
    is passed in while appending. Furthermore This ToStringStyle will only generate valid JSON if referenced objects also produce JSON when calling
    `toString()` on them.

    Since:
    :   3.4

    See Also:
    :   * [json.org](https://www.json.org/)

  * ### appendInternal

    protected void [appendInternal](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/ToStringStyle.html#line-1476)([StringBuffer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuffer.html "class or interface in java.lang") buffer,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") fieldName,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") value,
    boolean detail)

    Appends to the `toString` an [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang"), correctly interpreting its type.

    This method performs the main lookup by Class type to correctly route arrays, [`Collection`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Collection.html "class or interface in java.util")s, [`Map`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Map.html "class or interface in java.util")s and [`Objects`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Objects.html "class or interface in java.util") to the appropriate
    method.

    Either detail or summary views can be specified.

    If a cycle is detected, an object will be appended with the `Object.toString()` format.

    Parameters:
    :   `buffer` - the [`StringBuffer`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuffer.html "class or interface in java.lang") to populate.
    :   `fieldName` - the field name, typically not used as already appended.
    :   `value` - the value to add to the `toString`, not `null`.
    :   `detail` - output detail or not.

# Class CompareToBuilder

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.CompareToBuilder

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Builder<Integer>`

---

public class [CompareToBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-97)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [Builder](Builder.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")<[Integer](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Integer.html "class or interface in java.lang")>

Assists in implementing [`Comparable.compareTo(Object)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Comparable.html#compareTo-T- "class or interface in java.lang") methods.

It is consistent with `equals(Object)` and
`hashCode()` built with [`EqualsBuilder`](EqualsBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") and
[`HashCodeBuilder`](HashCodeBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder").

Two Objects that compare equal using `equals(Object)` should normally
also compare equal using `compareTo(Object)`.

All relevant fields should be included in the calculation of the
comparison. Derived fields may be ignored. The same fields, in the same
order, should be used in both `compareTo(Object)` and
`equals(Object)`.

To use this class write code as follows:

```
 public class MyClass {
   String field1;
   int field2;
   boolean field3;

   ...

   public int compareTo(Object o) {
     MyClass myClass = (MyClass) o;
     return new CompareToBuilder()
       .appendSuper(super.compareTo(o)
       .append(this.field1, myClass.field1)
       .append(this.field2, myClass.field2)
       .append(this.field3, myClass.field3)
       .toComparison();
   }
 }
```

Values are compared in the order they are appended to the builder. If any comparison returns
a non-zero result, then that value will be the result returned by `toComparison()` and all
subsequent comparisons are skipped.

Alternatively, there are [`reflectionCompare`](#reflectionCompare(java.lang.Object,java.lang.Object)) methods that use
reflection to determine the fields to append. Because fields can be private,
`reflectionCompare` uses [`AccessibleObject.setAccessible(boolean)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/reflect/AccessibleObject.html#setAccessible-boolean- "class or interface in java.lang.reflect") to
bypass normal access control checks. This will fail under a security manager,
unless the appropriate permissions are set up correctly. It is also
slower than appending explicitly.

A typical implementation of `compareTo(Object)` using
`reflectionCompare` looks like:

```
 public int compareTo(Object o) {
   return CompareToBuilder.reflectionCompare(this, o);
 }
```

The reflective methods compare object fields in the order returned by
[`Class.getDeclaredFields()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html#getDeclaredFields-- "class or interface in java.lang"). The fields of the class are compared first, followed by those
of its parent classes (in order from the bottom to the top of the class hierarchy).

Since:
:   1.0

  * ### CompareToBuilder

    public [CompareToBuilder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-331)()

    Constructor for CompareToBuilder.

    Starts off assuming that the objects are equal. Multiple calls are
    then made to the various append methods, followed by a call to
    [`toComparison()`](#toComparison()) to get the result.
* ## Method Details

  * ### reflectionCompare

    public static int [reflectionCompare](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-159)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") lhs,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") rhs)

    Compares two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s via reflection.

    Fields can be private, thus `AccessibleObject.setAccessible`
    is used to bypass normal access control checks. This will fail under a
    security manager unless the appropriate permissions are set.

    * Static fields will not be compared
    * Transient members will be not be compared, as they are likely derived
      fields
    * Superclass fields will be compared

    If both `lhs` and `rhs` are `null`,
    they are considered equal.

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - left-hand side object
    :   `rhs` - right-hand side object

    Returns:
    :   a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as `lhs`
        is less than, equal to, or greater than `rhs`

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if either (but not both) parameters are
        `null`
    :   `ClassCastException` - if `rhs` is not assignment-compatible
        with `lhs`

  * ### reflectionCompare

    public static int [reflectionCompare](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-227)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") lhs,
    [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") rhs,
    boolean compareTransients,
    [Class](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Class.html "class or interface in java.lang")<?> reflectUpToClass,
    [String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang")... excludeFields)

    Compares two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s via reflection.

    Fields can be private, thus `AccessibleObject.setAccessible`
    is used to bypass normal access control checks. This will fail under a
    security manager unless the appropriate permissions are set.

    * Static fields will not be compared
    * If the `compareTransients` is `true`,
      compares transient members. Otherwise ignores them, as they
      are likely derived fields.
    * Compares superclass fields up to and including `reflectUpToClass`.
      If `reflectUpToClass` is `null`, compares all superclass fields.

    If both `lhs` and `rhs` are `null`,
    they are considered equal.

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - left-hand side object
    :   `rhs` - right-hand side object
    :   `compareTransients` - whether to compare transient fields
    :   `reflectUpToClass` - last superclass for which fields are compared
    :   `excludeFields` - fields to exclude

    Returns:
    :   a negative integer, zero, or a positive integer as `lhs`
        is less than, equal to, or greater than `rhs`

    Throws:
    :   `NullPointerException` - if either `lhs` or `rhs`
        (but not both) is `null`
    :   `ClassCastException` - if `rhs` is not assignment-compatible
        with `lhs`

    Since:
    :   2.2 (2.0 as `reflectionCompare(Object, Object, boolean, Class)`)

  * ### append

    public [CompareToBuilder](CompareToBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [append](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-373)(boolean[] lhs,
    boolean[] rhs)

    Appends to the `builder` the deep comparison of
    two `boolean` arrays.
    1. Check if arrays are the same using `==`
    2. Check if for `null`, `null` is less than non-`null`
    3. Check array length, a shorter length array is less than a longer length array
    4. Check array contents element by element using [`append(boolean, boolean)`](#append(boolean,boolean))

    Parameters:
    :   `lhs` - left-hand side array
    :   `rhs` - right-hand side array

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

    public [CompareToBuilder](CompareToBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") [append](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/CompareToBuilder.html#line-763)([Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang") lhs,

    Appends to the `builder` the comparison of
    two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s.
    1. Check if `lhs == rhs`
    2. Check if either `lhs` or `rhs` is `null`,

    Appends to the `builder` the comparison of
    two [`Object`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")s.
    1. Check if `lhs == rhs`
    2. Check if either `lhs` or `rhs` is `null`,
       a `null` object is less than a non-`null` object
    3. Check the object contents

    If `lhs` is an array, array comparison methods will be used.
    Otherwise `comparator` will be used to compare the objects.
    If `comparator` is `null`, `lhs` must
    implement [`Comparable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Comparable.html "class or interface in java.lang") instead.

# Interface Diffable<T>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of objects that this object may be differentiated against

Functional Interface:
:   This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.

---

[@FunctionalInterface](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public interface [Diffable](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/Diffable.html#line-42)<T>

[`Diffable`](Diffable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") classes can be compared with other objects
for differences. The [`DiffResult`](DiffResult.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") object retrieved can be queried
for a list of differences or printed using the [`DiffResult.toString()`](DiffResult.html#toString()).

The calculation of the differences is *consistent with equals* if
and only if `d1.equals(d2)` implies `d1.diff(d2) == ""`.
It is strongly recommended that implementations are consistent with equals
to avoid confusion. Note that `null` is not an instance of any class
and `d1.diff(null)` should throw a [`NullPointerException`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/NullPointerException.html "class or interface in java.lang").

[`Diffable`](Diffable.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") classes lend themselves well to unit testing, in which a
easily readable description of the differences between an anticipated result and
an actual result can be retrieved. For example:

```
 Assert.assertEquals(expected.diff(result), expected, result);
```

Since:
:   3.3

# Class RecursiveToStringStyle

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

[org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

org.apache.commons.lang3.builder.RecursiveToStringStyle

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`

Direct Known Subclasses:
:   `MultilineRecursiveToStringStyle`

public class [RecursiveToStringStyle](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/RecursiveToStringStyle.html#line-55)
extends [ToStringStyle](ToStringStyle.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder")

Works with [`ToStringBuilder`](ToStringBuilder.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.builder") to create a "deep" `toString`.

To use this class write code as follows:

```
 public class Job {
   String title;
   ...
 }

 public class Person {
   String name;
   int age;
   boolean smoker;
   Job job;

   ...

   public String toString() {
     return new ReflectionToStringBuilder(this, new RecursiveToStringStyle()).toString();
   }
 }
```

This will produce a toString of the format:
`Person@7f54[name=Stephen,age=29,smoker=false,job=Job@43cd2[title=Manager]]`

Since:
:   3.2

# Interface Builder<T>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of object that the builder will construct or compute.

All Known Implementing Classes:
:   `BasicThreadFactory.Builder`, `CompareToBuilder`, `DiffBuilder`, `EqualsBuilder`, `HashCodeBuilder`, `ReflectionDiffBuilder`, `ReflectionToStringBuilder`, `StrBuilder`, `ToStringBuilder`, `TypeUtils.WildcardTypeBuilder`

Functional Interface:
:   This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.

---

[@FunctionalInterface](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/FunctionalInterface.html "class or interface in java.lang")
public interface [Builder](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/Builder.html#line-75)<T>

The Builder interface is designed to designate a class as a *builder*
object in the Builder design pattern. Builders are capable of creating and
configuring objects or results that normally take multiple steps to construct
or are very complex to derive.

The builder interface defines a single method, [`build()`](#build()), that
classes must implement. The result of this method should be the final
configured object or result after all building operations are performed.

It is a recommended practice that the methods supplied to configure the
object or result being built return a reference to `this` so that
method calls can be chained together.

Example Builder:

```
 class FontBuilder implements Builder<Font> {
     private Font font;

     public FontBuilder(String fontName) {
         this.font = new Font(fontName, Font.PLAIN, 12);
     }

     public FontBuilder bold() {
         this.font = this.font.deriveFont(Font.BOLD);
         return this; // Reference returned so calls can be chained
     }

     public FontBuilder size(float pointSize) {
         this.font = this.font.deriveFont(pointSize);
         return this; // Reference returned so calls can be chained
     }

     // Other Font construction methods

     public Font build() {
         return this.font;
     }
 }
```

Example Builder Usage:

```
 Font bold14ptSansSerifFont = new FontBuilder(Font.SANS_SERIF).bold()
                                                              .size(14.0f)
                                                              .build();
```

Since:
:   3.0

  `FluentBitSet()`

  Creates a new bit set.

  `FluentBitSet(int nbits)`

  Creates a bit set whose initial size is large enough to explicitly represent bits with indices in the range `0`
  through `nbits-1`.

  `FluentBitSet(BitSet set)`

  Creates a new instance for the given bit set.

    public [FluentBitSet](FluentBitSet.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.util") [and](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-76)([BitSet](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/BitSet.html "class or interface in java.util") set)

    Performs a logical **AND** of this target bit set with the argument bit set. This bit set is modified so that each
    bit in it has the value `true` if and only if it both initially had the value `true` and the
    corresponding bit in the bit set argument also had the value `true`.

    Parameters:
    :   `set` - a bit set.

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

  * ### nextSetBit

    public int [nextSetBit](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-340)(int fromIndex)

    Returns the index of the first bit that is set to `true` that occurs on or after the specified starting index.
    If no such bit exists then `-1` is returned.

    To iterate over the `true` bits in a [`BitSet`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/BitSet.html "class or interface in java.util"), use the following loop:

    ```
     for (int i = bs.nextSetBit(0); i >= 0; i = bs.nextSetBit(i+1)) {
         // operate on index i here
         if (i == Integer.MAX_VALUE) {
             break; // or (i+1) would overflow
         }
     }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `fromIndex` - the index to start checking from (inclusive).

    Returns:
    :   the index of the next set bit, or `-1` if there is no such bit.

    Throws:
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the specified index is negative.

  * ### previousSetBit

    public int [previousSetBit](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-415)(int fromIndex)

    Returns the index of the nearest bit that is set to `true` that occurs on or before the specified starting
    index. If no such bit exists, or if `-1` is given as the starting index, then `-1` is returned.

    To iterate over the `true` bits in a [`BitSet`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/BitSet.html "class or interface in java.util"), use the following loop:

    ```
     for (int i = bs.length(); (i = bs.previousSetBit(i-1)) >= 0; ) {
         // operate on index i here
     }
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `fromIndex` - the index to start checking from (inclusive)

    Returns:
    :   the index of the previous set bit, or `-1` if there is no such bit

    Throws:
    :   `IndexOutOfBoundsException` - if the specified index is less than `-1`

  * ### stream

    public [IntStream](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/stream/IntStream.html "class or interface in java.util.stream") [stream](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-527)()

    Returns a stream of indices for which this [`BitSet`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/BitSet.html "class or interface in java.util") contains a bit in the set state. The indices are returned
    in order, from lowest to highest. The size of the stream is the number of bits in the set state, equal to the value
    returned by the [`cardinality()`](#cardinality()) method.

    The bit set must remain constant during the execution of the terminal stream operation. Otherwise, the result of the
    terminal stream operation is undefined.

    Returns:
    :   a stream of integers representing set indices.

    Since:
    :   1.8
  * ### toByteArray

    public byte[] [toByteArray](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-546)()

    Returns a new byte array containing all the bits in this bit set.

    More precisely, if:

    1. `byte[] bytes = s.toByteArray();`
    2. then `bytes.length == (s.length()+7)/8` and
    3. `s.get(n) == ((bytes[n/8] & (1<<(n%8))) != 0)`
    4. for all `n < 8 * bytes.length`.

    Returns:
    :   a byte array containing a little-endian representation of all the bits in this bit set
  * ### toLongArray

    public long[] [toLongArray](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/util/FluentBitSet.html#line-565)()

    Returns a new byte array containing all the bits in this bit set.

    More precisely, if:

    1. `long[] longs = s.toLongArray();`
    2. then `longs.length == (s.length()+63)/64` and
    3. `s.get(n) == ((longs[n/64] & (1L<<(n%64))) != 0)`
    4. for all `n < 64 * longs.length`.

    Returns:
    :   a byte array containing a little-endian representation of all the bits in this bit set

    Performs a logical **XOR** of this bit set with the bit set argument. This bit set is modified so that a bit in it
    has the value `true` if and only if one of the following statements holds:
    * The bit initially has the value `true`, and the corresponding bit in the argument has the value
      `false`.
    * The bit initially has the value `false`, and the corresponding bit in the argument has the value
      `true`.

    Parameters:

    Returns:
    :   `this` instance.

* ## Method Details

  * ### acceptReadLocked

    public void [acceptReadLocked](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/concurrent/locks/LockingVisitors.LockVisitor.html#line-309)([FailableConsumer](../../function/FailableConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<[O](LockingVisitors.LockVisitor.html "type parameter in LockingVisitors.LockVisitor"),?> consumer)

    Provides read (shared, non-exclusive) access to The object to protect. More precisely, what the method
    will do (in the given order):
    1. Obtain a read (shared) lock on The object to protect. The current thread may block, until such a
       lock is granted.
    2. Invokes the given [`consumer`](../../function/FailableConsumer.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"), passing the locked object as the parameter.
    3. Release the lock, as soon as the consumers invocation is done. If the invocation results in an error, the
       lock will be released anyways.

    Parameters:
    :   `consumer` - The consumer, which is being invoked to use the hidden object, which will be passed as the
        consumers parameter.

    See Also:
    :   * [`acceptWriteLocked(FailableConsumer)`](#acceptWriteLocked(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableConsumer))
        * [`applyReadLocked(FailableFunction)`](#applyReadLocked(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableFunction))

    3. Release the lock, as soon as the consumers invocation is done. If the invocation results in an error, the

  * ### applyReadLocked

    public <T> T [applyReadLocked](../../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/concurrent/locks/LockingVisitors.LockVisitor.html#line-370)([FailableFunction](../../function/FailableFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<[O](LockingVisitors.LockVisitor.html "type parameter in LockingVisitors.LockVisitor"),T,?> function)

    Provides read (shared, non-exclusive) access to The object to protect for the purpose of computing a
    result object. More precisely, what the method will do (in the given order):
    1. Obtain a read (shared) lock on The object to protect. The current thread may block, until such a
       lock is granted.
    2. Invokes the given [`function`](../../function/FailableFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function"), passing the locked object as the parameter,
       receiving the functions result.
    3. Release the lock, as soon as the consumers invocation is done. If the invocation results in an error, the
       lock will be released anyways.
    4. Return the result object, that has been received from the functions invocation.

    *Example:* Consider that the hidden object is a list, and we wish to know the current size of the
    list. This might be achieved with the following:

    ```
     private Lock<List<Object>> listLock;

     public int getCurrentListSize() {
         final Integer sizeInteger = listLock.applyReadLocked(list -> Integer.valueOf(list.size));
         return sizeInteger.intValue();
     }
    ```

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - The result type (both the functions, and this method's.)

    Parameters:
    :   `function` - The function, which is being invoked to compute the result. The function will receive the
        hidden object.

    Returns:
    :   The result object, which has been returned by the functions invocation.

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalStateException` - The result object would be, in fact, the hidden object. This would extend
        access to the hidden object beyond this methods lifetime and will therefore be prevented.

    See Also:
    :   * [`acceptReadLocked(FailableConsumer)`](#acceptReadLocked(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableConsumer))
        * [`applyWriteLocked(FailableFunction)`](#applyWriteLocked(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableFunction))

The [`Processor.Arch`](Processor.Arch.html "enum in org.apache.commons.lang3.arch") enum defines the architecture of
a microprocessor. The architecture represents the bit value
of the microprocessor.
The following architectures are defined:

* 32-bit
* 64-bit
* Unknown

    public static <T,
    E extends [Throwable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Throwable.html "class or interface in java.lang")> T[] [fill](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/ArrayFill.html#line-170)(T[] array,
    [FailableIntFunction](function/FailableIntFunction.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.function")<? extends T,E> generator)
    throws E

    Fills and returns the given array, using the provided generator supplier to compute each element. Like
    [`Arrays.setAll(Object[], IntFunction)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Arrays.html#setAll-T:A-java.util.function.IntFunction- "class or interface in java.util") with exception support.

    If the generator supplier throws an exception, it is relayed to the caller and the array is left in an indeterminate
    state.

    Type Parameters:
    :   `T` - type of elements of the array.
    :   `E` - The kind of thrown exception or error.

    Parameters:
    :   `array` - array to be initialized.
    :   `generator` - a function accepting an index and producing the desired value for that position.

    Returns:
    :   the input array

    Throws:
    :   `E` - Thrown by the given `generator`.

    Since:
    :   3.18.0

    See Also:
    :   * [`Arrays.setAll(Object[], IntFunction)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Arrays.html#setAll-T:A-java.util.function.IntFunction- "class or interface in java.util")

Package [org.apache.commons.lang3.time](package-summary.html)

# Class FastDateParser

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateParser

All Implemented Interfaces:
:   `Serializable`, `DateParser`

---

public class [FastDateParser](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParser.html#line-87)
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")
implements [DateParser](DateParser.html "interface in org.apache.commons.lang3.time"), [Serializable](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/io/Serializable.html "class or interface in java.io")

FastDateParser is a fast and thread-safe version of [`SimpleDateFormat`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html "class or interface in java.text").

To obtain a proxy to a FastDateParser, use [`FastDateFormat.getInstance(String, TimeZone, Locale)`](FastDateFormat.html#getInstance(java.lang.String,java.util.TimeZone,java.util.Locale)) or another variation of the factory methods of
[`FastDateFormat`](FastDateFormat.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.time").

Since FastDateParser is thread safe, you can use a static member instance:

`private static final DateParser DATE_PARSER = FastDateFormat.getInstance("yyyy-MM-dd");`

This class can be used as a direct replacement for [`SimpleDateFormat`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html "class or interface in java.text") in most parsing situations. This class is especially useful in multi-threaded
server environments. [`SimpleDateFormat`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html "class or interface in java.text") is not thread-safe in any JDK version, nor will it be as Sun has closed the
[bug](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-4228335)/RFE.

Only parsing is supported by this class, but all patterns are compatible with SimpleDateFormat.

The class operates in lenient mode, so for example a time of 90 minutes is treated as 1 hour 30 minutes.

Timing tests indicate this class is as about as fast as SimpleDateFormat in single thread applications and about 25% faster in multi-thread applications.

Since:
:   3.2

See Also:
:   * [`FastDatePrinter`](FastDatePrinter.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3.time")

  * ### parse

    public [Date](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") [parse](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParser.html#line-1049)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") source,
    [ParsePosition](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/ParsePosition.html "class or interface in java.text") pos)

    This implementation updates the ParsePosition if the parse succeeds. However, it sets the error index to the position before the failed field unlike the
    method [`SimpleDateFormat.parse(String, ParsePosition)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/SimpleDateFormat.html#parse-java.lang.String-java.text.ParsePosition- "class or interface in java.text") which sets the error index to after the failed field.

    To determine if the parse has succeeded, the caller must check if the current parse position given by [`ParsePosition.getIndex()`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/ParsePosition.html#getIndex-- "class or interface in java.text") has been updated.
    If the input buffer has been fully parsed, then the index will point to just after the end of the input buffer.

    Specified by:
    :   `parse` in interface `DateParser`

    Parameters:
    :   `source` - A [`String`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang"), part of which should be parsed.
    :   `pos` - A [`ParsePosition`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/ParsePosition.html "class or interface in java.text") object with index and error index information
        as described above.

    Returns:
    :   A [`Date`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Date.html "class or interface in java.util") parsed from the string. In case of error, returns null.

    See Also:
    :   * [`DateParser.parse(String, java.text.ParsePosition)`](DateParser.html#parse(java.lang.String,java.text.ParsePosition))
  * ### parse

    public boolean [parse](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/FastDateParser.html#line-1068)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") source,
    [ParsePosition](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/text/ParsePosition.html "class or interface in java.text") pos,
    [Calendar](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/Calendar.html "class or interface in java.util") calendar)

    Parses a formatted date string according to the format. Updates the Calendar with parsed fields. Upon success, the ParsePosition index is updated to
    indicate how much of the source text was consumed. Not all source text needs to be consumed. Upon parse failure, ParsePosition error index is updated to
    the offset of the source text which does not match the supplied format.

    Specified by:
    :   `parse` in interface `DateParser`

    Parameters:
    :   `source` - The text to parse.
    :   `pos` - On input, the position in the source to start parsing, on output, updated position.
    :   `calendar` - The calendar into which to set parsed fields.

    Returns:
    :   true, if source has been parsed (pos parsePosition is updated); otherwise false (and pos errorIndex is updated)

    Throws:
    :   `IllegalArgumentException` - when Calendar has been set to be not lenient, and a parsed field is out of range.

    public static [TimeZone](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html "class or interface in java.util") [getTimeZone](../../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/TimeZones.html#line-76)([String](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html "class or interface in java.lang") id)

    Delegates to [`TimeZone.getTimeZone(String)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html#getTimeZone-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.util"), on Java 25 and up, maps an ID if it's a key in [`ZoneId.SHORT_IDS`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/ZoneId.html#SHORT_IDS "class or interface in java.time").

    On Java 25, calling [`TimeZone.getTimeZone(String)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html#getTimeZone-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.util") with an ID in [`ZoneId.SHORT_IDS`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/ZoneId.html#SHORT_IDS "class or interface in java.time") writes a message to [`System.err`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/System.html#err "class or interface in java.lang") in the form:

    ```
     WARNING: Use of the three-letter time zone ID "the-short-id" is deprecated and it will be removed in a future release
    ```

    You can disable mapping from [`ZoneId.SHORT_IDS`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/time/ZoneId.html#SHORT_IDS "class or interface in java.time") by setting the system property `"TimeZones.mapShortIDs=false"`.

    Parameters:
    :   `id` - Same as [`TimeZone.getTimeZone(String)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html#getTimeZone-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.util").

    Returns:
    :   Same as [`TimeZone.getTimeZone(String)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/TimeZone.html#getTimeZone-java.lang.String- "class or interface in java.util").

    Since:
    :   3.20.0

# Class AppendableJoiner<T>

[java.lang.Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

org.apache.commons.lang3.AppendableJoiner<T>

Type Parameters:
:   `T` - the type of elements to join.

---

public final class [AppendableJoiner](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/AppendableJoiner.html#line-84)<T>
extends [Object](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Object.html "class or interface in java.lang")

Joins an array or [`Iterable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Iterable.html "class or interface in java.lang") into an existing [`Appendable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang") like a [`StringBuilder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuilder.html "class or interface in java.lang"); with the goal for call sites to avoid creating
intermediary Strings. This is like [`String.join(CharSequence, CharSequence...)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#join-java.lang.CharSequence-java.lang.CharSequence...- "class or interface in java.lang"), [`String.join(CharSequence, Iterable)`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/String.html#join-java.lang.CharSequence-java.lang.Iterable- "class or interface in java.lang"), and [`StringJoiner`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/util/StringJoiner.html "class or interface in java.util").

Keep an instance in a (static) variable for efficient joining into an [`Appendable`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Appendable.html "class or interface in java.lang") or [`StringBuilder`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/StringBuilder.html "class or interface in java.lang") without creating temporary Strings.

Use the builder and instance methods to reuse the same kind of joining prefix, suffix, delimiter, and string conversion.

For example:

```
 // A reuseable instance
 private static final AppendableJoiner<Object> JOINER = AppendableJoiner.builder()
     .setPrefix("[")
     .setSuffix("]")
     .setDelimiter(", ")
     .get();
 
 ...
 // Builds straight into a StringBuilder:
 StringBuilder sbuilder = new StringBuilder("1");
 JOINER.join(sbuilder, "A", "B");
 sbuilder.append("2");
 JOINER.join(sbuilder, "C", "D");
 sbuilder.append("3");
 // Returns "1[A, B]2[C, D]3"
 return sbuilder.toString();
 }
```

To provide a custom Object element to [`CharSequence`](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/CharSequence.html "class or interface in java.lang") converter, call [`AppendableJoiner.Builder.setElementAppender(FailableBiConsumer)`](AppendableJoiner.Builder.html#setElementAppender(org.apache.commons.lang3.function.FailableBiConsumer)), for example:

```
 private static final AppendableJoiner<Item> JOINER = AppendableJoiner.builder()
     .setElementAppender(e -> (a, e) -> a.append(e.getFoo())
                                        a.append(e.getBar())
                                        a.append('!'))
     ...
     .get();
 
 }
```

This class is immutable and thread-safe.

Since:
:   3.15.0

    public static [DoubleRange](DoubleRange.html "class in org.apache.commons.lang3") [of](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/DoubleRange.html#line-48)(double fromInclusive,
    double toInclusive)

    Creates a range with the specified minimum and maximum values (both inclusive).

    The range uses the natural ordering of the elements to determine where values lie in the range.

    The arguments may be passed in the order (min, max) or (max,min). The getMinimum and getMaximum methods will return the correct values.

    Parameters:
    :   `fromInclusive` - the first value that defines the edge of the range, inclusive.
    :   `toInclusive` - the second value that defines the edge of the range, inclusive.

    Returns:
    :   the range object, not null.
  * ### of

    [Double](https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/lang/Double.html "class or interface in java.lang") toInclusive)

    Creates a range with the specified minimum and maximum values (both inclusive).

    The range uses the natural ordering of the elements to determine where values lie in the range.

    The arguments may be passed in the order (min, max) or (max,min). The getMinimum and getMaximum methods will return the correct values.

  * ### fit

    public double [fit](../../../../src-html/org/apache/commons/lang3/DoubleRange.html#line-105)(double element)

    Fits the given value into this range by returning the given value or, if out of bounds, the range minimum if
    below, or the range maximum if above.

    ```
     LongRange range = LongRange.of(16, 64);
     range.fit(-9) -->  16
     range.fit(0)  -->  16
     range.fit(15) -->  16
     range.fit(16) -->  16
     range.fit(17) -->  17
     ...
     range.fit(63) -->  63
     range.fit(64) -->  64
     range.fit(99) -->  64
    ```

    Parameters:
    :   `element` - the element to test.

    Returns:
    :   the minimum, the element, or the maximum depending on the element's location relative to the range.

    Since:
    :   3.19.0

* RISCV
